cultural.vision_reason: The image shows a rattan carrying-basket with woven headstrap, explicitly attributed by the museum to Kelabit makers using named local materials (rabun rattan, kilid bark string, tamar grass headstrap) — a classic Bornean household/utility item consistent with Kelabit craft.

physical.title: carrying-basket
physical.summary: Basket (bekang dechur) with headstrap (sengoloh), constructed with flap at front attached at the bottom, with closely woven rattan at back, and wooden piece attached to the bottom with rattan. Front and flap made of whole pieces of rattan twisted and intertwined into a pattern, within a frame of larger rattan. Coiled and intertwined rattan base. Made of rabun rattan (ue rabun), kilid bark string (anit kayuh kilid), and headstrap made of tamar grass (da'un tamar).
